On compute, he notes that "self driving cars require about 2,500 Watts of power for computation", while "a human brain only requires 20 Watts" <Cite id="brooks-better-lesson-2019" />. edits.before: The bet here is division of labor: a vision-language model decomposes goals into subtasks, and learned skills or a low-level policy execute them. SayCan (2022) had a separate LLM dispatch a fixed skill library <Cite id="saycan-2022" />; today the hierarchy sits inside the network or in a paired fast system ([hierarchical approaches](/manipulation/hierarchical/)). Google DeepMind builds Gemini Robotics ER 2 as a high-level brain that plans multi-step tasks and hands motor execution to a lower-level VLA <Cite id="gemini-robotics-er2-2026" />. In Figure's Helix 02, S2 interprets scenes and language and sequences behaviors. S1 converts perception into full-body joint targets at 200 Hz, and S0 executes at 1 kHz as the <Term id="whole-body-control">whole-body controller</Term> <Cite id="helix-02-2026" />. NVIDIA's GR00T N1 is "a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model with a dual-system architecture" <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />.

edits.before: A safety integrity level and a performance level are both assigned to a safety function <Cite id="iso-13849-1-2023" />, and both presume two things. The first is a verifiable specification: a statement of what the function must do, against which an implementation can be checked. The second is the avoidance of systematic faults, the design and specification errors that redundant hardware cannot remove and that the standards attack with process requirements.

Both presume a verifiable specification of what the function must do, and a development process that avoids systematic faults, the design errors that redundant hardware cannot remove.

edits.before: The formal instance is the safety filter. A <Term id="control-barrier-function">control barrier function</Term> defines a set the system must stay inside and turns forward invariance of that set into a constraint on the commanded input, enforced each step <Cite id="ames-cbf-2019" />. Wabersich and colleagues survey the family, including reachability and predictive variants, and describe a filter that takes a proposed input from any source and modifies it as little as necessary <Cite id="wabersich-safety-filters-2023" />. The guarantee belongs to the filter whatever produced the proposal, which is why the policy may stay unverifiable.

edits.before: The industrial instance is cruder and far more widely deployed: force limiting in the actuator, velocity limiting in the drive, and workspace limiting in the safety controller. The standards above know how to rate those mechanisms, whatever generated the trajectory. Agility describes Digit 5 in these terms: an independent safety controller oversees its response to people within an unsafe distance <Cite id="agility-digit-5-2026" />. edits.before: A position paper from October 2026 asks for the same kind of evidence on the human side of the interaction. Niccolò Pagliarani, Maximilian Stölzle, Daniela Rus, Matteo Cianchetti and colleagues argue that a claim that a robot is trustworthy around people should rest on evidence for three properties in the intended setting: bounded physical risk, behavior that people can anticipate, and expectations that match what the robot has shown it can and cannot do. In their view these should guide design and evaluation from the outset, and the paper offers candidate evaluation criteria as a research agenda, with no new measurements <Cite id="trustworthy-physical-ai-2026" />.
